issues: Event 1 reads '1838: Schleiden and Schwann: all living things are made of one or more cells'. EB dates Schleiden to 1838 (plants) and Schwann to 1839 (extended it to animals); the figure merges two people and two dates into 1838 and credits the general 'all living things' statement to that year.

Only 2 timeline events are drawn, but EB says three separate contributions built the generalisation in sequence (Schleiden 1838, Schwann 1839, Virchow 1855); the plant -> animal -> 'cells only from cells' progression is lost.
verdicts.fix: Timeline 1838-1855 with 3 events: '1838 - Schleiden: plants are built from cells'; '1839 - Schwann: extended to animals, so all organisms are built from one or more cells'; '1855 - Virchow: omnis cellula e cellula - cells arise only from pre-existing cells (rules out spontaneous generation of NEW cells today; says nothing about how the first cells arose)'.

issues: Group 'Animal cell only' lists only absences ('No cell wall', 'No chloroplast', 'Small/no vacuole'). EB's animal-specific structures (centrioles, lysosomes) are missing, so a group titled 'only' contains nothing animal cells actually have.

verdicts.fix: Three groups of positive structures. 'Shared by both' (membrane-bound organelles = compartmentalisation): Plasma membrane; Membrane-bound nucleus; Mitochondria; Endoplasmic reticulum; Golgi apparatus; Ribosomes. 'Plant cell (additionally)': Cellulose cell wall; Chloroplasts (absent from non-photosynthetic plant cells, e.g. roots); Large central vacuole. 'Animal cell (additionally)': Centrioles; Lysosomes. Replace the three 'No ...' items with these.

issues: Wrong part-whole level: the whole is 'Nuclear envelope' but three of the five parts ('Centromere', 'Telomere', 'Sister chromatids') are features of a condensed/replicated chromosome, not parts of the nuclear envelope.

'Chromatin' and 'Sister chromatids' / 'Centromere' are shown as simultaneously present static parts, but EB's central point is that chromosome structure is state-dependent: loose chromatin for most of the cell's life; condensed chromosomes only when preparing to divide; one chromatid before S phase, two sister chromatids joined at the centromere after replication.
EB's opening facts are not shown: the envelope is a double membrane with nuclear pores (mRNA out, proteins in). Karyotype / 46 chromosomes as 23 pairs is also absent.
verdicts.fix: Two linked structures. (1) Whole = Nucleus (boundary: Nuclear envelope, a double membrane). Parts: Nuclear pores (regulate traffic: mRNA out, proteins in); Nucleolus (rRNA synthesis, ribosome-subunit assembly); Chromatin (DNA wrapped on histones, loosely packed and transcriptionally accessible most of the cell's life). (2) Whole = Condensed chromosome (forms when the cell prepares to divide). Parts: Sister chromatids (two identical copies, present only after S-phase replication; a single chromatid before S); Centromere (joins the sister chromatids); Telomeres (protective repetitive caps at both ends). Optional note: humans have 46 chromosomes = 23 pairs (22 autosome pairs + XX/XY); a karyotype is the full ordered set.

issues: Stage 2 'Smooth ER: the smooth endoplasmic reticulum synthesises lipids and processes the protein further' is false for the protein route: secretory proteins pass from the rough ER (via vesicles) to the Golgi; the smooth ER makes lipids and detoxifies and is not a stage in the protein pathway. The chain 'Rough ER -> Smooth ER -> Golgi apparatus' misrepresents the route.
No ER-to-Golgi transport vesicle is drawn; the only vesicle shown buds from the Golgi. EB: vesicles bud off the ER and carry cargo to the Golgi.

EB's central corrective claim is missing and step 1 implies the opposite: 'ribosomes on the rough endoplasmic reticulum synthesise the protein' suggests every protein starts here. EB: only secretory-pathway proteins (membrane, secreted, lysosomal) are made on rough-ER ribosomes (signal sequence); cytoplasmic proteins are made on free ribosomes and never enter this system.
Final stage 'Lysosome / secretion' merges two different destinations; vacuoles (storage, plant turgor) are absent.
verdicts.fix: Ordered pathway (linear): 'Rough ER' (ribosomes directed by a signal sequence make secretory, membrane and lysosomal proteins into the ER lumen) -> 'Transport vesicle' (buds from the ER, carries cargo to the Golgi) -> 'Golgi apparatus' (receives, modifies by glycosylation, SORTS and dispatches) -> destinations: 'Lysosome' (acid hydrolases digest delivered material) / 'Plasma membrane or secretion'. Drop 'Smooth ER' as a stage; show it as a side annotation (synthesises lipids, detoxifies) and add Vacuole (stores water/nutrients/waste; plant central vacuole maintains turgor). Add a note: cytoplasmic proteins are made on free ribosomes and never enter this pathway.

issues: NAD+ regeneration - which EB states is fermentation's essential function ('regenerate NAD+ from NADH ... allowing glycolysis to CONTINUE') - appears nowhere in the figure; fermentation is shown only as a 'Low ATP yield' variant of respiration, which is the misconception EB corrects.

'Low ATP yield' is attached to the 'Lactic acid fermentation' and 'Alcoholic fermentation' groups as if fermentation produces the ATP; per EB the 2 ATP/glucose come from glycolysis and fermentation itself adds no net ATP.
Glycolysis - the oxygen-independent step common to all three routes - is not shown, so the reason O2 matters (final electron acceptor of oxidative phosphorylation) is not conveyed.
verdicts.fix: Keep the three columns but add the defining function. 'Aerobic respiration': glycolysis -> pyruvate oxidation -> citric acid cycle -> oxidative phosphorylation (needs O2 as final electron acceptor); ~30-32 ATP per glucose. Common first step: 'Glycolysis (no O2 needed): net 2 ATP, converts NAD+ to NADH'. 'Lactic acid fermentation' (muscle in intense exercise; lactic acid bacteria): pyruvate -> lactate in one step, regenerating NAD+. 'Alcoholic fermentation' (yeast): pyruvate -> ethanol + CO2 in two steps, regenerating NAD+. Replace the fermentation 'Low ATP yield' items with 'Purpose: regenerate NAD+ so glycolysis keeps running' and 'No net ATP beyond glycolysis (2 ATP/glucose total)'.

issues: EB's essential content - each adhesion family's specific binding logic (cadherins: homophilic cell-cell, Ca2+-dependent; selectins: transient 'catch-and-roll' binding to carbohydrates; integrins: cell-to-matrix binding fibronectin/collagen) - is collapsed into one node 'Adhesion molecules: cadherins, selectins and integrins hold cells together and to the matrix' with no partner or function information.

Wrong structure type: three coexisting, non-interchangeable adhesion families are drawn as stage 1 of a process ('Adhesion molecules' -> 'Epithelial-mesenchymal transition'), implying adhesion molecules turn into EMT. The families belong in a comparison/hub; only EMT -> outcomes is a process.
verdicts.fix: Split into two. (A) Comparison, three groups: 'Cadherins' - cell-to-cell, homophilic (bind identical cadherin on adjacent cell), calcium-dependent, hold same-type cells together; 'Selectins' - transient weaker cell-to-cell adhesion by binding specific carbohydrates, 'catch-and-roll' e.g. white blood cells on vessel walls; 'Integrins' - cell-to-extracellular-matrix, bind fibronectin/collagen, anchor the cell to its scaffold. (B) Pathway: 'Epithelial cell (adherent, polarised sheet)' -> 'EMT (reversible: loses cell-cell adhesion via reduced cadherin function, and apical-basal polarity; becomes mobile)' -> branch to 'Normal: gastrulation, wound healing (then MET restores epithelium)' and 'Pathological: cancer cells detach, invade, metastasise'.

issues: Template polarity labels are inverted relative to the drawn synthesis. Top template is labelled 3' at the parental/fork end (label '3′' at (-5,1.7)) and 5' at the free right end (label '5′' at (5,3)); bottom is 5' left / 3' right. Yet the leading strand is drawn on the TOP template, built 5'->3' leftwards toward the fork from a primer at its right end. A strand grown 5'->3' toward the fork has its 3' end at the fork, so it can only be antiparallel to a template whose 5' end is at the fork. As labelled, the new strand would run parallel to its template.

By the real rule the leading-strand template is read 3'->5' in the direction of fork movement, so its 3' end is at the free (replicated) end. The labelled top template has its 3' end at the parental end, i.e. it is the lagging-strand template; likewise the bottom label makes it the leading one.

Self-contradiction: step 2 says 'the top template runs 3′ to 5′ away from the fork, the bottom one 5′ to 3′', but step 4 says on the top template 5'->3' 'points toward the fork' and step 5 says on the bottom template 5'->3' 'points away from the fork'; both are true only if the labels in step 2 are the other way round. The figure therefore teaches the central 5'->3' / antiparallel logic of leading vs lagging strands inconsistently.

Source pointer (read-only observation): src/lib/teaching/sceneGenerators/dnaReplication.pure.ts - header GEOMETRY comment, the four label('3′'/'5′') calls near lines 88-91, and the narrations near lines 145-147 and 163.
verdicts.fix: Swap the four polarity labels: parental end top '5′', parental end bottom '3′'; free (right) end top '3′', free end bottom '5′'. Step 2 narration: 'Each separated strand is now a template. They run in opposite directions: the top template runs 5′ to 3′ away from the fork (its 3′ end is at the free end), the bottom one 3′ to 5′.' Keep steps 3-6 as is (primer at the top template's 3′ free end; DNA polymerase builds the leading strand 5′->3′ continuously toward the fork; on the bottom template Okazaki fragments are built 5′->3′ away from the fork from new primers nearer the fork, joined by ligase; semiconservative summary). Also correct the header GEOMETRY comment and the one-line scene summary ('the top one 3′ to 5′ from the fork, the bottom one 5′ to 3′').

issues: No 'Hypothesis' stage: EB's sequence is observation -> hypothesis (specific, testable, falsifiable explanation) -> controlled experiment. The figure folds it into the Observation narration ('prompts a specific, testable hypothesis'), so the central object of the method is never a step.

Drawn as an open one-way chain. EB stresses that a falsified hypothesis is a valuable result that narrows the explanations (so the next move is to revise and retest) and that findings are only provisionally trusted until replicated; no return/feedback path exists.

Final node merges 'Replication and peer review' with narration 'independent researchers reproduce the result; experts scrutinise methods before publication' - peer review precedes publication and replication follows it, so the combined order is muddled.
verdicts.fix: Pathway with a feedback loop (cyclic/return path): 'Observation' -> 'Hypothesis (specific, testable, falsifiable)' -> 'Controlled experiment (vary exactly one independent variable; hold control variables constant; measure the dependent variable; compare with a control group)' -> 'Statistical evaluation (adequate sample size; could chance explain the result?)' -> 'Peer review (independent experts scrutinise methods/conclusions - a necessary check)' -> 'Independent replication (other researchers obtain the same result) -> provisionally accepted'. Return path: 'Hypothesis falsified or not replicated -> revise explanation and retest (a falsified hypothesis is a genuine, valuable result)'.
